sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in Moline, Illinois?
sections.html:
You can list it with an agent, sell it yourself, or sell it to a buyer who pays cash and accepts the house in its current condition. The fastest closings come from the third route, though the offer will be priced for the work the house needs.

Moline is a Quad Cities city, and the buyers who show up here are shaped by that. Some are workers tied to the large employers along the river, some are investors, and some are families moving within the Illinois and Iowa sides of the metro. Knowing which group your house suits helps you choose the route.

The sections below cover the local facts that affect a sale: the city's housing numbers, its neighborhoods and school districts, the building and code offices, and the recorder steps in Rock Island County.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Moline's housing?
sections.html:
Moline is the largest city in Rock Island County. The 2020 Census counted 42,985 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 42,362, which is 1.4 percent below the 2020 estimates base.

The housing profile for 2020 to 2024 is distinct from the Chicago suburbs. Median owner-occupied value is $146,300, and median gross rent is $900. About 67.3 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, and the city has 18,289 households averaging 2.29 people. Median household income is $67,701 and the mean commute is only 18.0 minutes.

  • Lower prices mean a repair bill can take a bigger share of the sale price, so scope the work before you decide to renovate.
  • A short commute and a large employment base make renting out a house a realistic option for some owners, and buyers who rent houses out may bid on yours.
  • With the population estimate slightly below 2020, buyers have choices, and a house that needs work may sit longer on the open market.

sections.h2: Which Moline neighborhoods and school districts do buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Moline sits on a bluff between the Mississippi and Rock rivers, and deep ravines cut the high ground into natural neighborhoods. Neighborhood associations work with the city, and the downtown area is known as Moline Centre.

Other neighborhood names in common use include Floreciente, Olde Towne, Uptown, Overlook, Karsten's Park, Wharton, Hamilton Heights, Wildwood, Prospect Park, Tartan Oaks, Park Hill, Forest Hill, Highland, Villa Park, Green Acres, Rockview Estates, Homewood, Heritage Park, Stewartville, Deerview and Walton Hills. A listing that names the neighborhood reads more clearly to local buyers than a street address alone.

Most of the city is in Moline School District No. 40, which runs twelve elementary schools, John Deere Middle School, Woodrow Wilson Middle School and Moline High School. Parts of the city fall in East Moline School District 37 with United Township High School District 30, and in Rock Island-Milan School District 41. Check which district a specific address belongs to before you quote one in an ad.

sections.h2: How do Moline's roads, river and employers shape demand?
sections.html:
Interstate 74 runs straight through the city and splits it into two roughly equal halves, and Interstate 280 circles the Quad Cities. The new I-74 bridge over the Mississippi opened with a ribbon-cutting on December 1, 2021. Moline is about 165 miles west of Chicago.

Deere and Company keeps its corporate headquarters in Moline, and Kone's U.S. division is based in the city as well. Black Hawk College and the Quad Cities campus of Western Illinois University are both in Moline, and Quad Cities International Airport sits on the south edge of town. South Park Mall and a string of big-box centers make the city the retail hub of the Illinois side.

The downtown arena, Vibrant Arena at The MARK, and John Deere Commons draw events that fill nearby restaurants and hotels. Houses within a short drive of these destinations tend to be pitched to commuters and renters, so say so in your listing.

sections.h2: Does Moline's climate affect what a buyer will inspect?
sections.html:
Moline has hot, humid summers and cold winters. The long-run average is 23 days a year at 90 degrees or higher, 43 days when the high stays at or below freezing, and 11 days with lows below zero. Snow averages 31.6 inches per season.

Buyers will check the roof, the furnace and the air conditioner, because a house here works both systems hard. The freeze-thaw cycle also tests sidewalks, driveways and foundation walls. The long-run record puts freezing temperatures from about October 10 to April 24, so exterior work is easiest to schedule outside that window.

Houses on bluffs and ravine edges also deserve a look at drainage and grading. If a lot slopes toward the foundation, expect an inspector to flag it.

sections.h2: What does the City of Moline require, and who do you call?
sections.html:
The Building and Inspections Division is at the City Services Center, 1830 6th Avenue, and visitors use the north entrance on 6th Avenue. It handles building permits and plan reviews, building inspections, contractor registration, food establishment licensing and code enforcement.

Code complaints about housing, nuisance, vegetation, zoning and signs go through the City's Neighborhood Improvement Officer, who also works with the neighborhood groups. If your house has an open complaint or a citation, resolve it or ask the city what a closing needs, because a title company can discover it.

  • Pull permit records for any remodel, deck, roof or mechanical work done in your years of ownership.
  • Ask the division how to close out any permit that was opened but never finished.
  • Ask the water and sewer divisions about final billing before the closing date.

The city publishes its Code of Ordinances online for anyone who wants to check a rule before listing.

sections.h2: How does a deed get recorded in Rock Island County?
sections.html:
Deeds for Moline houses are recorded by the Rock Island County Recorder, 1504 3rd Avenue, second floor, in Rock Island. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and can be reached at 309-558-3360.

The office states that documents must be on 8.5 by 11 inch white paper with a blank 3 by 5 inch space in the upper right corner of the first page, nothing stapled or taped to it, and at least 10-point type in black ink. Each document must show who prepared it and where to return it, and a deed must also show the grantee's address and a mail-tax-bill-to address.

Illinois sets a state transfer tax of 50 cents per $500 of value in 35 ILCS 200/31-15. Ask the Recorder whether any county or city stamp applies on top of it.

sections.h2: What should a Moline seller prepare before accepting an offer?
sections.html:
Complete the disclosure report first. Under 765 ILCS 77/20 a seller of residential property fills out every item on the statutory report and delivers it to the buyer before the contract is signed.

Next, gather the paperwork a closing needs: the parcel number, your latest property tax bill, a mortgage payoff statement if there is a loan, and any permit records. If the house is a rental, collect the leases and tenant contact details, because a buyer will want to see them.

Compare at least two offers on net proceeds, not just the headline price. Ask each buyer who pays the transfer stamps, what repairs they expect, and how many days they need to close.

faqs.q: Is Moline a fast market for selling a house?
faqs.a: It depends on the house. Moline's median owner-occupied value of $146,300 is low compared with Chicago suburbs, and the population estimate is down slightly from 2020, so a house that needs work can take longer on the open market. A direct sale to a cash buyer is the quickest route.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Moline house?
faqs.a: At the Rock Island County Recorder's Office, 1504 3rd Avenue, second floor, Rock Island, Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The phone number is 309-558-3360.

faqs.q: What must be on a deed before Rock Island County will record it?
faqs.a: The county asks for 8.5 by 11 inch white paper, a blank 3 by 5 inch space at the top right of the first page, black ink in at least 10-point type, and preparer and return-to information. A deed also needs the grantee's address and a mail-tax-bill-to address.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for work on my Moline house?
faqs.a: Most building work needs one. The Building and Inspections Division reviews plans, issues permits, inspects work and registers contractors, so contact the division at the City Services Center before starting a project.

faqs.q: What does Illinois require me to give a buyer?
faqs.a: A completed residential real property disclosure report, delivered before the contract is signed, under 765 ILCS 77/20. The state transfer tax of 50 cents per $500 of value is collected when the deed is recorded.
